reason: The cited evidence shows stress relief and recrystallization in HEAs only under very different conditions (1100 °C for minutes in E1, 400 °C for 2.5 hours in E2), not the proposed 1–2 second in-situ laser scan. Neither passage supports the claim that such a brief, moderate-temperature treatment can induce partial recrystallization or effectively relieve stresses in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi, leaving the key premises unsupported.
premises: Localized reheating to 300–400 °C for 1–2 seconds can induce partial recrystallization and stress relief in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Short-duration, moderate-temperature annealing relieves thermal mismatch stresses while preserving a fine-grained microstructure.
In-situ annealing after each LPBF layer will significantly reduce residual thermal stresses compared to conventional processing.
Reduced residual stresses will lead to improved ductility and fatigue resistance in miniature components.
